_comment: UI glyphs: the handful of game images that are not any one record's icon.
WHY A LIST AND NOT A SCRAPER. Every other family here is harvested from a
real association — an item's `Items.icon` column, a villager's infobox, a
`link=` target a human wrote next to the file. These have no such anchor.
The tesserae glyph appears inline inside price strings; the season glyphs
appear inside the `season` column's markup. A scraper for them would be
pattern-matching on presentation, which changes without notice and fails
silently. Twenty-odd names written down is both less code and less wrong.
WHERE THE NAMES CAME FROM. Each one was read out of committed wikitext in
sources/, not guessed from a convention. `pnpm assets:fetch` 404s loudly on
a name that does not exist, so a wiki rename surfaces as a failed fetch
rather than as a missing image nobody notices.
`key` is ours and becomes `ui/<key>`; the app asks for that and never for a
filename. `file` is the wiki's, verbatim.
Deliberately absent: mine biome icons. All five biomes link the same
Fp_wiki_mining.png, so adopting it would render five distinct places
identically — strictly worse than five distinct generated glyphs.
MAPS AND BRAND. `maps` is the DataMaps background image the committed Map: page
declares — the 5442x3599 space every anchor already lives in. `brand` is the
game logo from the main page infobox, used (framed in our own mark) as the app
icon. Both ship as loose files, never atlased.
